description: Cauldrons and concoctions - a healer who throws potions and turns Spirit into healing power.
_source_note: Rebuilt 5 Nov 2026 from the 37 real CoA Brewing talents (role Healer, 'Primarily Restoration Shaman, with Mistweaver Monk and a touch of Warlock'). Replaces a 23-node tree with 4 procs. Brewing is a LOADOUT spec in CoA - Ingredients brewed into a Cauldron decide what Potion Toss does - and this engine has no mode state a talent can read or set, no ground-placed object with a radius, and no party aura. Frontier already has every brew as a castable party ability, so talents that buff a named brew port cleanly; the three Mojo swaps, Tiki Splash and Unstable Concoction do not and say so per node. Spirit Healer ports whole - both conversions are legal pairs.

nodes.name: Spirit Healer
nodes.description: Increases your healing power by 25% of your Spirit and your spell critical strike chance by 9% of your Spirit.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Level 20 Passive. Increases healing power by 25% of Spirit and increases spell critical strike chance by 10% of Spirit.' PORTS WHOLE, which is rare for a conversion node - healing_power AND crit_chance_spell are both in STAT_CONVERSION_TARGETS and spirit is in STAT_CONVERSION_SOURCES. Compare Voodoo Power on the DPS tree, whose spell-hit half had to be dropped because hit_rating is not a target. Both are FRACTIONS.

nodes.name: Potent Mixes
nodes.description: Increases your healing done by 8% and reduces the threat your spells generate by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases your healing done by 4% and reduces the threat generated by your spells by -15%.' Doubled for the two ranks and authored as the full-investment ceiling. NOTE the two keys here take different units and are read twelve lines apart in entities/character.py - healing_power_pct is divided by 100 (line 1295) so 8.0 is 8%, while threat_generation_pct is a raw FRACTION where negative reduces.

nodes.name: Mojo Addiction
nodes.description: Increases your maximum mana by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases your maximum mana by 5%.' Doubled for the two ranks. max_mana_pct is a FRACTION - it is NOT divided by 100 (character.py:1419), unlike healing_power_pct on the node above it. 10.0 here would have been 1000% mana.

nodes.name: Presence of the Loa
nodes.description: Increases your spell critical strike chance by 3%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases your critical strike chance by 4%.' Routed to the spell side, since every ability this spec casts is a spell. PERCENT.

nodes.name: Fresh Ingredients
nodes.description: Increases the healing of Jungle Shrooms by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases the healing of your Jungle Shrooms from your Cauldron by 15%.' Doubled for the two ranks. 'From your Cauldron' is the loadout distinction CoA draws between a brewed and a thrown Ingredient, and there is no loadout state here - Jungle Shrooms is simply a party ability you cast, so the bonus applies whenever you cast it.

nodes.name: Mixologist
nodes.description: Increases the healing of your Ingredients by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA's own description for this node is the unresolved token '$40' - the Builder payload never expands it, so there is no verbatim text to port and this is NOT a faithful copy. Named for the spec's core skill and built as broad Ingredient effectiveness, which is what every other Mixologist-adjacent talent in the tree does (Potion Boss, Spice: Earthroot, Master Mixologist). Flagged so a later pass can correct it if the real text surfaces. All three Ingredients written out because no key names a group.

nodes.name: Plentiful Potions
nodes.description: Reduces the mana cost of Loa's Brew and Hexbreak by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Reduces the cost of your Loa's Brew and Hexbreak by -10%.' Both abilities exist in Frontier. POSITIVE reduces, so CoA's minus sign is dropped - authoring -0.10 here would have RAISED the cost.

nodes.name: Brewmaster
nodes.description: Increases the healing of Loa's Brew by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Reduces the cast time of Loa's Brew by 0.25 sec.' There are no cast times here, so nothing of this talent survives as written. Rerouted to the healing of the same ability, which is what a faster cast buys - more Loa's Brew throughput.

nodes.name: Spice: Earthroot
nodes.description: Increases the healing of your Ingredients and the Voodoo Cauldron by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Infuse your Cauldron with Spice: Earthbloom. Increases effectiveness of all Cauldron effects and Ingredients by 30%.' CoA's 30% kept. 'Cauldron effects' is read as the Voodoo Cauldron ability, the only Cauldron Frontier actually has as a thing you cast. Note CoA's own text disagrees with its node name - Earthroot in the title, Earthbloom in the body; the title is kept.

nodes.name: Disciple of Sseratus
nodes.description: Increases the healing of Loa's Brew and Spirit in a Bottle by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the bonus healing scaling of Loa's Brew and Spirit in a Bottle by 15%.' There is no key for how much an ability scales with healing power - the coefficients live on the abilities - so it is expressed as healing, which is what the scaling buys. Spirit in a Bottle is an enemy-target ability in Frontier that heals on hit, so the key is still live.

nodes.name: Potion Boss
nodes.description: Increases the healing of Potion Toss and Splash Potion by 12%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the effectiveness of Potion Toss and your tossed Ingredients by 20%.' Splash Potion stands in for 'tossed Ingredients', since a thrown Ingredient is not a separate thing here - there is no loadout, so an Ingredient is only ever cast directly.

nodes.name: Splash On 'Em
nodes.description: Your heals bring Potion Toss and Splash Potion a turn closer to ready.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Effective healing done by Loa's Brew and Mojo Beam reduce the cooldown of Potion Toss and Splash Potion by 1 sec.' Ports almost exactly - on_heal_cast is the right trigger and both target abilities exist. 1 sec becomes 1 turn, which is a buff relative to CoA, because a turn is roughly three seconds and a fraction of a turn cannot be expressed.

nodes.name: Touch of the Spirits
nodes.description: Spirit in a Bottle leaves the enemy taking 3% more damage and dealing 3% less for 5 turns.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Damage dealt by Spirit In a Bottle causes the enemies to take 3% more damage and deal -3% less damage for 15 sec.' Both halves live and 15 sec is 5 turns. THE TWO KEYS TAKE DIFFERENT UNITS INSIDE THE SAME STATUS EFFECT: bare damage_taken_pct is read RAW, so 3% is 0.03, while damage_dealt_pct is percentage POINTS, so -3% is -3.0. Authoring damage_taken_pct as 3.0 would mean 300% extra damage taken - the same key that produced immortality on Boltslinger's Evasive when it was authored at -20.0.

nodes.name: Spice: Peacebloom
nodes.description: Reduces the duration of stuns against you by 24%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Infuse your Cauldron with Spice: Peacebloom. Reduces the duration of roots, stuns, and snares against allies within 40 yds by -25%.' There is no party-aura mechanism, so the reduction lands on the Witch Doctor and the description says 'you' rather than promising an aura the engine will not deliver. Roots and snares are dropped from the description because the only key that exists, stun_duration_reduction_pct, is read solely against effects flagged is_stun (status_effects.py:699) - promising roots and snares would be text with no mechanic behind it. It is a FRACTION where POSITIVE reduces, floored so a stun can be shortened but never negated. CoA's 25% kept. My first draft invented 'cc_duration_taken_pct', which no engine code reads - caught by audit_talents.

nodes.name: Jungle Secrets
nodes.description: Loa's Brew splashes 35% of its healing onto the worst-off ally.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'When you heal with Loa's Brew your Effigies will now heal an additional ally within 20 yds for 35% of the healing done, prioritizing allies with low health.' Ports closely - splash_heal already prioritises the worst-off ally, which is exactly CoA's rule, and 35% and one extra target are CoA's numbers. The Effigy doing the healing is flavour; nothing here lets a summon carry a heal.

nodes.name: Unstable Concoction
nodes.description: Potion Toss splashes 40% of its healing across up to 3 nearby allies.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Potion Toss now applies Unstable Concoction to the target for 20 seconds. Using Loa's Brew or Spirit in a Bottle on the target will trigger an explosion of mojo around the target, healing nearby allies within 20 yds for 177 + 40% healing.' A DELAYED DETONATION keyed on a second ability hitting the same target, which needs two things the engine lacks: nothing reads whether a target carries a debuff, and no payload fires on a later specific cast. Built as an immediate splash off Potion Toss at CoA's 40%, so the healing lands without the setup step.

nodes.name: Master of Concoctions
nodes.description: Jungle Shrooms and Frog Bones last 1 turn longer, and your Ingredients heal 11% more.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the duration of Ingredients by 20% and causes allies affected by Jungle Shrooms to heal for 5% of the damage they deal with their next 3 offensive abilities or spells for 15 sec.' The leech-on-allies half would need a party-wide applied buff with a charge counter, and neither the aura nor the charges exist. The duration half is built as a flat turn on the two Ingredients that have one, plus the 20% as effectiveness. NOTE the small integer durations keep this node out of the rank policy's reach - see tools/talent_ranks.rankable().

nodes.name: Doctor of the Jungle
nodes.description: Increases the healing of Jungle Shrooms by 12%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Jungle Shrooms used from your Cauldron now ticks -2 sec faster.' A faster tick has no meaning when ticks are per-turn, so it is rerouted to healing, which is what a faster tick delivers - more healing in the same window.

nodes.name: Jungle Booms
nodes.description: Jungle Shrooms heal 53% more.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Jungle Shrooms used from your Cauldron now heal for 100% more, but heals 3 less targets.' CoA's 100% kept and THE DOWNSIDE IS DROPPED, because no key removes targets from an ability - the same wall that stops a key from adding them. So this node is strictly stronger than CoA's, which is noted rather than hidden: a single-target trade is the whole point of CoA's version and it cannot be expressed. Priced at one rank at tier 4 to keep it honest.

nodes.name: Mojo Wave
nodes.description: Mojo Beam reaches further, splashing 75% of its healing across up to 3 of the worst-off allies.
nodes._source: CoA's level 40 passive: 'Healing with Mojo Beam now heals up to 3 of the lowest health nearby allies for 75% of the healing done and casting it grants allies Replenishment. Replenishment Replenishes 5% of maximum mana per 5 sec for 15 seconds.' The splash half ports exactly - 75%, 3 targets, worst-off first, all CoA's. Replenishment is dropped: there is no per-turn mana regeneration key and no party aura. Frontier has Mojo Beam as an ability already, so this is not its unlock.

nodes.name: Base: Crystal Water
nodes.description: Your heals shield the target for 20% of the healing done.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Infuse your Cauldron with Crystal Water for 10 sec, causing party and raid members within 40 yds to be shielded for 20% of their healing taken for 5 sec. Only 1 Base can be active at a time.' Frontier HAS Base: Crystal Water as a castable ability, so this talent is the passive version: CoA's 20% of healing as a shield, applied by your own heals rather than by a Cauldron with a radius, and permanently rather than in a 10-second window. 'Only 1 Base at a time' has no state to enforce. shield_pct is a FRACTION.

nodes.name: Base: Beast Blood
nodes.description: Reduces the physical damage you take by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Infuse your Cauldron with Beast Blood for 10 sec, causing 15% of the direct Physical damage taken by party and raid members within 40 yds to instead be dealt over time.' Converting a hit into a dot on someone else is not a mechanic here - nothing redirects or defers incoming damage - and there is no party aura. Built as straight physical mitigation for the Witch Doctor at CoA's 15%, which is the survivability the talent buys. As a TALENT effect physical_damage_taken_pct is a fraction where NEGATIVE reduces; inside a status effect the same key is divided by 100 and positive increases.

nodes.name: Voodoo Cauldron
nodes.description: Increases the healing the Voodoo Cauldron does by 27% and the healing you receive by 6%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Place down a Voodoo Cauldron for 15 sec, increasing allies' healing received by 20% while near the cauldron. Allies within 15 yds are healed for 300+Heal*0.6 every 1.5 sec for 15 sec.' Frontier has Voodoo Cauldron as a castable party ability, so this talent empowers it. The healing-received aura has no party mechanism, so half of CoA's 20% lands on the Witch Doctor alone. AS A TALENT EFFECT healing_taken_pct is a FRACTION, so 10% is 0.10 - inside a status effect the same key is percentage POINTS. Authoring 10.0 here would have been 1000%, which is what shipped briefly on Bloodmage Eternal.

nodes.name: Loa's Blessing
nodes.description: Your heals bless you with the Loa's favour, raising your haste by 3% and the healing you receive by 3% for 5 turns, stacking 3 times.
nodes._source: CoA's level 30 passive: 'Healing done by Loa's Brew now applies a RANDOM empowerment to the target ally. Ferocity of Bethekk increases melee, ranged and spell haste by 3%. Vitality of Sseratus healing received increased by 3%. Cunning of Quetz'lun critical strike...' A random pick from a table is not a payload - apply_effect takes one effect, or a list, but nothing chooses among them - so the buff grants two of CoA's three empowerments at once, at CoA's own 3% each, and lands on the caster because a proc buff cannot be sent to the heal's target. INSIDE A STATUS EFFECT healing_taken_pct is percentage POINTS, so 3% is 3.0 - the opposite unit to the same key on the node beside it.

nodes.name: Sen'jin's Presence
nodes.description: Reduces the mana cost of Loa's Brew by 21%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Casting Potion Toss and Spirit in a Bottle now reduce the cast time of your next 2 Loa's Brews by 20% for 10 sec.' Three things fail at once: no cast times, no charge counter, and no payload that discounts a later specific cast. Rerouted to a flat cost reduction on the same ability at CoA's 20%, which is the throughput the talent buys. POSITIVE reduces.

nodes.name: Master Mixologist
nodes.description: Your heals crit 10% more often and your Ingredients, Cauldron and potions all heal 21% more.
nodes._source: CoA: 'For 10 sec, the effectiveness of all Cauldron effects and Ingredients is increased by 100% and you can cast Spirit in a Bottle while moving.' Frontier HAS Master Mixologist as a castable self ability, so this talent is its passive half. Casting while moving is positional. CoA's 100% in a 10-second window on a 2-minute cooldown is priced at a permanent 40% plus crit - roughly the same throughput averaged out, and reachable every turn rather than once a fight. The three Mojo talents that would also have lived at this tier (Mojo: Fish Bones, Frog Shrooms, Jungle Thistle) are NOT built: each resets a cooldown and then swaps the loaded Ingredient pair, and there is no loadout state to swap. Tiki Splash is dropped for the same reason - it transforms one ability into another while a Base is active, and there is no 'while active' gate.

nodes.name: Potent Brew
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike damage of your spells by 20% per rank.
nodes._source: Authored 6 Nov. Kyle: 'all caster classes should have a 5 point talent that increases their spell crit damage by 100%.' Mirrors priest_shadow's Shadow Power and shaman_elemental's Elemental Fury, both of which are WoW-accurate at 5 x 20%. Placed on tier 4 beside the existing tier-4 block; connected_to is cosmetic (it draws the edge), spending is gated by tier_requirements.
